text:
devin: Folks — following up on the RFC: we need a short decision on fused dequant + attention vs keeping dequant separate. main constraints: streaming tail p99, KV cache memory, and support for fp8 (e4m3/e5m2), int8, int4. Thoughts?

sara: My take: fused dequant+attention kernels are the best for batch throughput and peak memory, but they complicate streaming (append-only KV) because you can't dequantize incrementally without extra copies. tradeoff is latency vs memory. :thinking:

mike: Data from microbench (internal): fused (fp8) gave ~+18-25% throughput and ~30% GPU mem reduction on long sequences (seq_len=4096) vs separate dequant then GEMM. p99 not great for single-stream.

nina: Streaming concern is real. For single active stream, extra kernel latency for fused may add ~0.8-1.5ms at tail when KV grows. Users with low concurrency will see worse p99. We should provide a hybrid policy.

devin: Hybrid = keep cache quantized but expose two execution paths? e.g., when concurrency>1 or batch>1 use fused; when concurrency==1 use dequant-to-cache path that keeps a small dequant window?

eva: Proposed API/config knobs (high level):

```json
{
  "dequant_strategy": "auto | fused | on_write",
  "cache_format": "quantized | dequantized",
  "scale_mode": "per_head | per_tensor",
  "streaming_threshold": 0.75
}
```

sara: Implementation notes: keep KV in quantized layout (packed INT8/FP8) in GPU mem. Add a fused kernel that reads quantized KV + queries -> performs dequant internally and computes attention without writing a full dequantized KV. That avoids extra mem allocations. For streaming, implement "on_write" which dequantizes appended tokens into a small dequant cache region (sliding window) so tail queries hit dequantized data.

mike: Also need per-head scale support for INT8/INT4. experiments show per-head scales reduce bias and improve quality for Llama-family models. perf cost is small if fused kernel handles scale multiply cheaply.

nina: Edge case: FP8 variants (e4m3 vs e5m2) have different exponent ranges — must normalize scales and test for overflow on kv dot-products. Add fast-paths for hw that supports FP8 fused FMA (a100x + special libs) otherwise fallback to mixed FP16 path.

devin: Suggest kernel-selection pseudo-code to drive runtime routing: 

```python
# kernel selection (pseudocode)
if model.quant in ("fp8_e4m3","fp8_e5m2") and hw.has_fp8_fma:
    if streaming and config.dequant_strategy == "on_write":
        select("fp8_fused_dequant_attention_on_write")
    elif batch_size > 1 or concurrency > 1:
        select("fp8_fused_dequant_attention")
    else:
        select("fp8_mixed_fp16_attention")  # lower tail latency
elif model.quant == "int8":
    if config.scale_mode == "per_head":
        select("int8_perhead_fused_attention")
    else:
        select("int8_global_fused_attention")
else:
    select("fp16_attention")
```

sara: Good. Also we need a stable ABI between runtime and kernels: input layout descriptors (scale pointers, qkv strides, cache format flag) so kernels can be swapped without changing higher layers. Keep descriptor small and immutable per model load.

eva: Testing + rollout plan:
- unit tests: numerical bit-exactness tolerance vs fp16 baseline on short sequences
- regression evals: prompt sets + rouge/accuracy checks (quality delta < 0.5%)
- perf canary: Dedicated -> 5% traffic, monitor token p50/p95/p99, GPU mem, and error rates
- fallback: on quality or latency regression, auto-switch model to fp16 path and alert

infra-bot: Canary job created: canary/dequant-fused-v1 on dedicated cluster (5% traffic). Monitor metrics: inference.p99_latency, inference.token_throughput, model.quality.delta. :rocket:

mike: Ops note: need instrumentation points in runtime to measure dequant time vs attention time. add histograms per kernel.

nina: Security: ensure quantized cache can't leak scale metadata between tenants. isolating per-tenant scale tables in device memory.

devin: Next steps: (1) PR with kernel-selector + descriptor (2) prototype fused fp8 kernel (3) perf runs and canary. I'll own the selector; sara+mike own kernel prototype. eva owns tests + rollout.

sara: I'll draft the ABI and config schema and drop a short PR tomorrow.

mike: I'll run perf matrix on A100, H100, and gpus without fp8 support to collect fallback numbers.

nina: I'll add streaming benchmarks (single-stream long seq) to ensure tail latency targets.

devin: Thanks. keeping this thread as the coordination point. tagging folks: @sara @mike @nina @eva. :thumbsup:
